name: Allstate Arena
heading: ACCESSIBILITY
passage: The Allstate Arena strives to provide excellent service to all our guests, including those guests with special needs. Allstate Arena recognizes the needs of persons with disabilities and meets or exceeds the requirements for compliance with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA). Allstate Arena provides a full range of accommodations for guests with disabilities to ensure their safety, comfort and enjoyment of our events and facilities. The following section highlights our services.

name: Allstate Arena
heading: ACCESSIBILITY
passage: Accessible/Disabled seating is available on the lower level of the arena. Wheelchair area is located behind sections 113 and 116 (depending on event set-up behind sections 105 and 108 may also be available). Wheelchairs must purchase a ticket to these areas only. There is no access to main floor or other seating areas. If you can walk with assistance tickets can be purchased in any section but wheelchair can’t be stored at or near your seat. Tickets for accessible seating areas are available through Ticketmaster and the Allstate Arena Box Office. When ordering tickets for an accessible seating area, it is important to indicate that you require accessible seating so we can properly seat you. Please note that the number of seats available in the accessible seating area meets the requirements of the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) and other laws relating to accessibility, however, the number of seats in the accessible seating areas is limited. Tickets for seats in the accessible seating areas are sold on a first come, first served basis.

name: Allstate Arena
heading: ACCESSIBILITY
passage: Allstate Arena provides complimentary wheelchair escorts to guests with special needs when requested. Escorts are available at any entry point. Please be aware that our staff will not remain with you during the event, nor will they allow you to remain in the wheelchair for the duration of the event.

heading: Onsite Courtesy Shuttles presented by Aurora Health Care®
passage: Courtesy shuttles are available for guests needing assistance at select pick-up locations around the American Family Field grounds. Please see the American Family Field Parking Map for Courtesy Shuttle locations. Shuttles will only pick up from these locations and drop guests at the nearest entrance to American Family Field. After games, shuttles will pick up guests who need assistance at the Robin Yount Statue on the Home Plate Plaza and next to the UW Credit Union Plaza Gate on the Center Field Plaza and return them to the original pick-up locations. Expect longer wait times on day games and highly attended games. This is a free service; tipping is not permitted.

name: American Family Field
heading: Autograph Sundays presented by efrutti
passage: Every Sunday home game from April through August, kids ages 14 and under are invited to meet and receive an autograph from a Brewers player, alumni and/or other Brewers personality from 11:50 a.m. – 12:10 p.m. at designated locations, which will be posted on the scoreboard when gates open. Player lineup and autograph times are subject to change. Autographs are limited to one per child and full-sized bats or other prohibited carry-in items are not allowed. Children needing assistance in accessing the autograph signings should visit the Guest Relations kiosk on the Field Level near Section 116 with their parent/guardian. A Guest Relations staff member will assist children in accessing the field.

name: American Family Field
heading: Batting Practice
passage: Fans are invited to watch batting practice from their seats once American Family Field gates open (please find details listed under “Gate Opening Times”). Batting practice is subject to cancellation without notice. For your safety, please do not lean on or over railings or nets to catch baseballs at any time, and please be aware of bats and balls that may enter the seating areas at any time players and/or coaches are on the field. Please find details listed under “Policies Relating to Guest Conduct” for information on the Flying Balls and Flying Bats policy.

name: American Family Field
heading: Designated Driver
passage: As part of our commitment to fan safety, we have partnered with Miller Lite, Delaware North, and Interstate Parking to implement a Designated Driver program at American Family Field. To register, the driver of a vehicle parked in the American Family Field lots must pledge not to consume alcoholic beverages while at American Family Field or in the American Family Field parking lots. The Designated Driver must be at least 21 years of age, have an American Family Field parking receipt or digital parking pass for that game, and a valid driver's license. The driver will receive one coupon for a complimentary soft drink. Participants may register at the Designated Driver kiosk located in the concourse behind Section 120 or at Brewers Guest Relations behind Section 419 from the time American Family Field gates open until one hour after the start of the game.

passage: The Angels strive to make every guest's visit to Angel Stadium enjoyable and accessible to persons with disabilities. The Angels have established the following pilot policy regarding Segways and similar devices in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act ("ADA") and California State Law.

name: Angel Stadium
heading: Angel Stadium Segway Usage Policy
passage: The Angels recommend that Segway users purchase tickets in one of the Stadium's accessible seating areas. Segway users may purchase tickets for up to 3 additional companion seats as outlined in the "Accessible Seating" for Guests with Disabilities section of the Angels' "A to Z Guide," including in the same seating locations as the wheelchair accessible seats. If more than one Segway guest will be in attendance together at a particular game, the Angels, at their sole discretion, may relocate users to the same section.

passage: Free limited accessible parking for guests with mobility impairments with a valid disability placard or other authorized identification is available in the drop-off circle adjacent to the Museum, located at 200 Hurd Road. name: Bethel Woods Center for the Arts
heading: General Accommodations
passage: Trained service animals are ALWAYS welcome at Bethel Woods Center for the Arts. Emotional support animals, comfort animals and therapy dogs are not permitted at Bethel Woods, as per Title III of the ADA. Consistent with ADA guidelines, Bethel Woods defines “service animal” as limited to a dog that is individually trained to work or perform tasks for an individual with a disability. The task(s) performed by the dog must be directly related to the individual’s disability. Bethel Woods requires, consistent with ADA, that service animals must be harnessed, leashed, or tethered, unless these devices interfere with the service animal’s work or the individual’s disability prevents him or her from using these devices. Individuals who cannot use such devices must maintain control of the animal through voice, signal, or other effective methods.

name: Broadview Stage at SPAC
heading: Additional Accommodations
passage: SPAC allows service animals to enter the venue. Service animals are defined by the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) as dogs or miniature horses that are trained to do work to perform tasks related to people with disabilities. The work or task the service animal is trained to do must directly relate to the person’s disability. Service animals must be housebroken. Service animals are required to behave and not repeatedly bark, growl, jump up on, or lunge at other guests or employees. Corrective action must be taken if the service animal is not behaving appropriately.

name: Broadview Stage at SPAC
heading: Additional Accommodations
passage: Dogs whose sole function is to provide comfort or emotional support do not qualify as service animals under the ADA. Comfort animals, emotional support animals, and therapy dogs are not listed as service animals under Title II and Title III of the ADA. This also applies to the other species of animals, wild or domestic, trained or untrained. The ADA requires the service animal to be under the control of the handler. This may include using a harness, leash, or other tether. Our venue employees are not required to provide for the care or supervision of a service animal, including cleaning up after it. Service animals must remain on the floor and are not allowed on dining chairs or tables in our food and beverage locations. Live Nation and our operating partners have the right to deny access to a service animal that disrupts our operations.

name: Citizens Bank Park
heading: Mobile Ticketing
passage: The MLB Ballpark app was upgraded with enhanced security features to protect your mobile tickets. Please update and log in BEFORE you leave for Citizens Bank Park to ensure your tickets and/or parking is ready to scan the moment you arrive. Click “Get Started” Manually enter your password You will then receive a 6-digit one-time code via email, enter that to verify your email address. Next you will be required to enroll your mobile number You will then receive a 6-digit one-time code via text message, enter that to verify your mobile number. Once verified, you will now be logged into the Ballpark app and should be able to access your tickets. After completing these steps, if you are unable to see or access your tickets in the Ballpark app, please call 215-463-1000 or email us at tickets@phillies.com .

name: Credit Union 1 Amphitheatre
heading: Accessible Parking
passage: Accessible Parking is located just outside of Gate 4 on the southwest side of the venue, in front of the Premier Parking lot. We'd recommend driving into the venue via South Road, through entrance 1. Upon arrival on event day, inform staff that you need accessible parking. Accessible spaces are limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis. Our parking crew will work to accommodate you if all accessible spaces are full. Fans may also be dropped off near the gates prior to parking. Credit Union 1 Amphitheatre honors any state-issued accessible parking placard for a vehicle that fits in a 9’ x 18’ parking space without impeding the people on either side of your vehicle. Oversized vehicles (e.g. stretch limos, RVs, buses, etc.) with a disabled parking placard will not be allowed to park in an accessible parking space. To ensure you can park as close as possible, we recommend arriving when the parking gates open.

heading: Accessible Information
passage: The Cross Insurance Center is one of the most adaptable and accessible entertainment venues in New England. Visiting the Cross Center for an event will not be an inconvenience. Let our professional, friendly staff assist you with any special needs to ensure that your event experience is enjoyable and memorable. The Cross Insurance Center was designed and built to accommodate our guests with special needs by complying with all ADA specifications. Below you will find information and services that we offer to our guests with disabilities and limitations. We encourage all guests who have concerns, comments, or who need assistance to talk to any member of the Cross Insurance Center staff. If any guests have further questions or have suggestions on how to make your experience more enjoyable please call us at 207.561.8300.

name: Cross Insurance Center
heading: Accessible Information
passage: We offer accessible parking in all parking areas located near the facility. The parking lot, located adjacent to the Renewal by Andersen Entrance of the facility will be the primary parking place for guests with disabilities. All guests who wish to park in the reserved spaces must have a state issued handicapped window pass, sticker, or license plate. Vehicles that do not have these credentials will be allowed to drop guests off at the Hammond Lumber Company Entrance [formerly Southeast Entrance] on Bass Park Blvd. and then proceed to the other parking lots or Hollywood Casino parking garage. There are also two other options for parking which accommodate parking for guests with disabilities – the Raceway Lot located up Bass Park Blvd. on the left and the Buck St. Lot located along the racetrack through the Buck St. entrance.

name: Dodger Stadium
heading: 50/50 Raffle
passage: The Los Angeles Dodgers Foundation (LADF) 50/50 Raffle is back for the 2026 season! From the time the gates open until the end of the seventh inning, fans may purchase raffle tickets from uniformed ticket sellers wearing pink 50/50 raffle aprons and stationary kiosks located throughout the concourses at the stadium. Here is your chance to win big, in the name of charity! Every game, 50% of the jackpot is awarded to one lucky winner and the remaining 50% supports LADF's programs and grantmaking to local nonprofit organizations. Purchase a 50/50 raffle ticket and support LADF!

passage: Alcohol is served from the time the stadium gates open to the public through the 7th inning. Alcohol is limited to a maximum of 2 alcoholic beverages per person per purchase. Alcohol may not be purchased by persons under the age of 21, according to California law. Proper identification with proof of age must be presented at time of sale. Alcohol sales may be discontinued at any time.

name: Dodger Stadium
heading: UNIQLO Field at Dodger Stadium Policies & Information
passage: Screenshots of tickets are not considered valid tickets and will not scan at the gates. You must present a valid mobile ticket (and not a screenshot) to be permitted entry into the stadium.

name: Dodger Stadium
heading: Ballpark app
passage: How to Enter a Dodger game at the stadium Simply have the Ballpark app open and pull up your ticket barcode for that day's game. If you're entering with a group, you have the option to scan multiple tickets on one device, use Go-Ahead Entry facial authentication technology at select gates, or forward tickets to your group in advance to be scanned via the Ballpark app on their devices. Having issues scanning in? Be sure to adjust your screen's brightness and watch out for glares from lights or the sun, both of which may prevent your mobile ticket from scanning properly. Making your way to your seats at the stadium? Simply show your Guest Service Representative your mobile ticket on the Ballpark app to be directed to your seat. Note: If you have both the Ballpark app as well as a printed ticket for the same seat, the first ticket scanned is the only one that will allow entry into the stadium. Once a ticket has been scanned, it cannot be forwarded.

name: Dodger Stadium
heading: Ballpark app
passage: How to Forward Tickets You can easily forward tickets via the Ballpark app by tapping the "Share" icon. Mobile tickets can be forwarded via email or a text link. When you forward a ticket, it will still appear on your list of tickets in the Ballpark app, but it will not feature a mobile barcode. Mobile tickets without barcodes cannot be used for entry into the stadium. You may choose to cancel a forwarded ticket and have it reinstated as a live mobile ticket in your Ballpark app. Instructions on how to cancel a forwarded ticket are provided on a later page.

name: Dodger Stadium
heading: Ballpark app
passage: EMAIL: To forward a single ticket via email, select that recipient's name from your device's address book or enter their email address directly. The recipient will be sent an email notifying them that you have sent mobile ticket(s). The recipient must click "Access Tickets" in that email in order to receive the ticket(s).

name: Dodger Stadium
heading: Ballpark app
passage: TEXT: If you do not know a recipient's email address, you can share a ticket via text message by selecting the "Forward via Link" option. Simply select that recipient from your address book or enter their mobile phone number. They will receive a text with a link to accept that mobile ticket.

name: Dos Equis Pavilion
heading: Accessible Parking
passage: Accessible parking is available at Dos Equis Pavilion. To park in an accessible parking space, you will need a valid, state-issued accessible placard or license plate and a venue parking pass. Parking passes can be purchased online via Ticketmaster in advance or on the day of the show with a credit card when you arrive at the parking lots. General parking will be $20 per vehicle (plus tax) online in advance and $25 on the event day. To use an accessible space, your vehicle must display a valid, state-issued accessible placard or license plate, and the person to whom the placard or plate is issued must be in the vehicle. Accessible parking areas are actively monitored, and credentials may be subject to inspection to prevent misuse. All applicable state and local laws apply. Misuse of an accessible space may result in citation, fines, or relocation.

name: Dos Equis Pavilion
heading: Accessible Parking
passage: Accessible spaces are limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis. Our parking crew will work to accommodate you if all accessible spaces are full. Fans may also be dropped off near the gates prior to parking. Dos Equis Pavilion has parking available on the East and West side of the venue, located off of South Fitzhugh Avenue. Turn on your emergency flashers to help parking staff identify your needs and they will direct you to the appropriate area. Guests in need of accessible parking should enter the following gates and check in with the parking attendant on where to park:

name: Dos Equis Pavilion
heading: Accessible Ticketing
passage: Accessible tickets can only be purchased online at dosequispavilion.com/shows . Our box office is not able to take ticket orders over the phone, and our website is the only method to purchase tickets. Accessible tickets are reserved solely for fans with disabilities and their companions. Fans who abuse this policy could have their order canceled.

name: Dos Equis Pavilion
heading: Accessible Ticketing
passage: To find tickets in the Accessible Seating Area of Dos Equis Pavilion, select the Filters icon on the upper right of the page where you see available tickets. For a reserved seated show, you will be shown your seat location once the ticket is selected. More information regarding the purchase of accessible seating on Ticketmaster can be found here . In a general admission event, the accessible seating area can reach capacity early and is first-come, first-served. Our Accessible section on the floor is located at the main walkway into the House, at the East and West side entrances. Upon entry, there will be an open area beside the rail that is available to Accessibility. If a chair is needed, guests can inquire with security in the area. Security will be on standby for the Accessibility section for the duration of the event.

name: Dos Equis Pavilion
heading: Accessible Ticketing
passage: Our accessible section of the lawn, located at the bottom of the lawn on the East and West corners, has reserved seating, in addition to a general admission area that is first-come, first-served. The lawn is uncovered and subjected to the elements. In inclement weather, the terrain can become difficult to navigate. Note: The Starplex Lawn Deck seats are accessible via staircase in the West Plaza only. There is a concrete ramp that goes halfway up the lawn, towards The Starplex Lawn Deck.

All requests for sign interpretation should be directed to the Accessible Seating line at 703-993-3035, or by emailing Lindsey Park (lbross@gmu.edu). name: EagleBank Arena
heading: A-Z Guide
passage: A general admission ticket to an EagleBank Arena event means there are no reserved seats and, in the case of a floor general admission ticket, there are no seats, only standing. Patrons with general admission floor tickets should assemble and enter at the North entrance. Entry of patrons is controlled and there is no running to seats or crowding at the doors. There are no chairs on the floor for general admission events; the floor is standing room only. For a concert where the floor is general admission, the permanent seats in the arena are usually RESERVED seats. On each general admission ticket there are numbers printed for “seat” and “row,” but these numbers are for ticketing inventory purposes only, and do not correspond to a location inside the building.

We take pride in our ballpark being accessible for everyone and ensuring our guests with disabilities have an enjoyable and comfortable experience. We are always looking for ways to improve our ballpark experience and the quality of each guest's visit, so your feedback and suggestions are vital to our success.

name: Kauffman Stadium
heading: Accessible Parking
passage: More than 500 reserved parking spaces are available to properly licensed or tagged vehicles for guests with disabilities. Spaces are available in all parking lots except Lot L and Lot N. A limited number of van-accessible spaces are available in each of these lots. Wheelchair ramps are present in all parking lots. The reserved spots are filled on a first-come, first-served basis. Guests with disabilities, or those persons transporting a guest with a disability, should notify Royals personnel of their desire to park in an accessible space. Those without the proper license tag or permit to park in a reserved space, but have someone who has trouble walking, should be directed to the nearest non- accessible parking space.

passage: Our Guest Ambassadors assist guests with special needs and disabilities to ensure a comfortable experience on game days. Für gewöhnlich ist das Backstage Restaurant von Einlass- bis zum Veranstaltungsbeginn geöffnet. Bei Sportveranstaltungen – darunter selbstverständlich alle Heimspiele der Kölner Haie – oder Events, bei denen es die Bühnenkonstruktion zulässt, ist das Backstage Restaurant auch während der gesamten Veranstaltungsdauer geöffnet.

heading: Pre-Kickoff Exit & Re-Entry Policy
passage: 6 p.m. or later start times, the Atrium is open to ticketed guests six hours prior to kickoff. heading: Persons under 18 years of age
passage: Events hosted by PROGRESJA are open for all people over 12 years old (with exception of those dedicated especially for kids and teens). Minors may enter the club with a written consent of their legal guardian ( FORM ), unless the club states otherwise at a specific event. Information regarding parental consent for a minor to attend a concert organized by Progresja is necessary for us to ensure the safety of event participants. We require that the child have a completed and signed consent form by their legal guardian, using the form available on our website, and we verify this during ticket inspection at the entrance to the concert. However, we DO NOT COLLECT, STORE, or PROCESS these forms or the personal data contained therein. We only want to ensure that the minor is participating in the event with the consent of their guardian, and we can contact them if necessary.This information applies to concerts organized by Progresja. name: M&T Bank Stadium
heading: Accessible (ADA) Seating and Parking
passage: Accessible (ADA) seating is available throughout the stadium on all levels. Guests who require ADA seating, including PSL Owners, should contact the Ticket Office at 410-261-RAVE (7283) to purchase those seats in advance. Seats are offered on a first-come, first-serve basis and ADA seating may not be available on game day. ADA parking is located in Lots B/C and Lot R (located off of the Russell Street Service Drive). ADA parking cannot be purchased in advance and is first come, first-serve. Access to disabled parking spaces is limited to vehicles with state-issued disabled license plates or valid disabled hangtags. In addition, the person to whom the disabled tag was issued must be in the vehicle and will be asked to provide a state MVA disabled registration card, state-issued identification and a valid game ticket. Parking lots will open 4 and a half hours prior to kickoff and tailgating is prohibited. Kits for guests with sensory disabilities are available at stadium guest services locations.

name: M&T Bank Stadium
heading: Multipurpose Rooms & Nursing Mothers
passage: Our Multipurpose Guest Service locations can be used for nursing mothers and/or guests with disabilities who might need to escape the elements during the game. These spaces are stocked with sensory items such as headphones, toys, etc., allowing a comfortable, quiet, private area for those that need it.

Throughout the game, it remains accessible to guests who have cloth wristbands that specify "Xfinity FlockYard Lofts," up until when North Plaza closes (up to 90 minutes post-game, subject to change game to game).

Re-entry into M&T Bank Stadium is not permitted.

The valet accepts bikes, personal e-scooters and e-bikes once gates open and will close 45 minutes after the completion of the game. heading: A to Z Guide

passage: Assistive Listening Devices (ALDs) technology in North Island Credit Union Amphitheatre is powered by Listen Everywhere Technology™. This allows you to use your mobile device and headphones as your personal ALD. If you do not wish to use your device, please see the guest services booth to get a receiver. A photo ID is required to be held until the device is returned at the end of the event. Please bring your own headphones or ear buds.

heading: Kulture City/Sensory Bags
passage: North Island Credit Union Amphitheatre is a KultureCity Certified Sensory Inclusive Venue. Please visit our Guest Services booth for more information. Our sensory bags are designed to support various sensory needs in both adults and children. To check out a sensory bag, visit our Guest Services booth, located in either plaza. Sensory bags include noise-reducing headphones, strobe glasses, fidget tools, and more!

passage: Please make your request by calling 619.494.5600 and include how many in your party need interpretation and the ticket type you have. passage: Tickets located in our accessible section can be purchased online at northislandcreditunionamp.com/shows. Please be advised that this is done on a first come, first served basis and our accessible seating area can reach capacity early. Our Accessible seating sections are located in Left Orchestra, Right Orchestra, Section 101 and 103, Section 201, 202, 204, and 205, Section 301 and 305, and the East side of the Lawn.

name: Oracle Park
heading: Bags, Containers & Coolers
passage: Backpacks (including clear backpacks) are NOT permitted inside Oracle Park. Accommodations are made for diaper bags, medical bags and guests with accessible needs. Otherwise this policy is strictly enforced and exceptions will not be made. Other bags, that do not exceed 16" x 16" x 8" in size, are permitted: paper and plastic grocery bags, purses, fanny packs, lunch bags, briefcases, diaper bags, soft-sided coolers, and handbags. Hard-sided coolers are not permitted. Bags do not need to be clear.

name: Oracle Park

passage: After every Sunday day game, weather permitting, children age 14 and under can run the bases. Please be aware of any particular circumstances that may affect this event such as a change in game time. Refer to the Giants current season schedule for any affected dates. Children and their parents must exit the ballpark after the game and re-enter at the right field viewing portal from the Portwalk. After guests have finished running the bases, they will be directed out of the ballpark by event staff behind home plate. The promotion is held at the discretion of management.

passage: Whenever possible, we’ll have a separate queue for Priority members. Up to three of your mates can join you too. Our staff, and the O2 Angels, will help you or just look out for the Priority queue signs or banners at the entrance.

passage: Your ticket should state the time the doors open, and the event page on our website will have the door time and curfew.

name: O2 Shepherds Bush Empire

passage: We can discuss suitable locations where your dog can stay throughout the show. Alternatively, if you would like your dog to be looked after, we'll arrange for someone to meet you at the entrance and guide you to your seat. Dogs will be looked after throughout the event in a quiet location with somewhere to lay with a bowl of water.

name: O2 Shepherds Bush Empire
heading: On Arrival
passage: If you need assistance or ramp access, let us know in advance and someone will meet you at Stage Door in Rockwood Place, at the side of the venue, just ask a member of our front of house staff to show you the way. We’d recommend arriving about 15 minutes before doors open, just to make things easier.

However, you may be able to drop off along Lane Avenue near St. John Arena (traffic can be very heavy at times) and then board the ADA shuttle to Ohio Stadium.

name: Ohio Stadium
heading: West Campus Shuttle
passage: NEW LOCATION: A complimentary shuttle service will transport guests from the West Campus Lots (Carmack Lots near Kenny Road & Woody Hayes Drive) to the Campus Transit Hub (located off John Herrick Drive near the Lincoln Tower fields). The West Campus pickup spot is in front of Mount Hall. The Transit Hub drop off is conveniently located just south of Ohio Stadium near the recreational tennis courts. This shuttle will operate from 6 hours prior kickoff until 1 hour after the game. The shuttles are large transit busses, which additionally have a wheelchair lift and can accommodate up to two wheelchairs at a time if needed.

Rideshares can pickup/dropoff along Borror Drive near the Schottenstein Center OR they may stop at 19th & Neil Avenue in Central Campus.

passage: Drivers from the vehicle company must remain with the vehicle, and the vehicle must remain on site at all times. Drivers & vehicles will not be permitted to exit the area and return later for a pickup.

name: Ohio Stadium
heading: Lost and Found at Ohio Stadium
passage: Lost and Found is located at 5A Guest Services and remains open for 30 minutes after the event. If you need to try to find your item after the event has ended and you have left the facility, submit a Lost Item Report online and we will try to match it up with the items that were found/logged. Reports will be viewed on the next business day (i.e. our facilities may be closed on the weekends). Found items that have been matched to your Lost Item Report will be mailed/shipped directly to you or can be held for pickup for 30 days following the event. Guests are responsible for the mailing/shipping fees. To search or report a lost item, please report it by submitting a Lost Item Report .

Drivers will not be able to pick you up near Ohio Stadium on event days due to traffic patterns and security checkpoints.

From there, the seats designated for wheelchair users and the regular seating areas can be easily reached. All wheelchair-accessible seats are located on the inner concourse in the East Curve (sections Q, R, S, T), in the Marathontor area (sections G, H, J, K), on the opposite grandstand in section N, and in the VIP grandstand.

name: Olympiastadion
heading: Accessibility at the Stadium
passage: People who use wheelchairs are warmly welcome to join our guided tours and visits to the Berlin Olympic Stadium. The five-star stadium is generally barrier-free and accessible to people with limited mobility. However, unrestricted mobility is not always possible within the seating sections; for example, the upper tier is accessible only by stairs.

passage: Animals or pets of any kind are prohibited at Pechanga Arena San Diego with the exception of trained service animals and service animals in training for guests with disabilities. Service animals are welcome inside the venue, but must, at all times, remain on a leash or in a harness. Service animals should rest in the seating area of the individual with a disability, rather than in the aisle. A guest whose service animal poses a threat to the safety of other Pechanga Arena San Diego guests and employees may be asked to escort the animal off the premises.

name: Progressive Field
heading: Re-Entry
passage: Fans needing to exit and re-enter Progressive Field must do so through a dedicated gate at the Left Field Gate. Their game ticket or seat locator will be scanned upon exit. To re-enter the Ballpark, fans will enter through the security checkpoint and turnstiles where their ticket or seat locator will be re-scanned. During the games in which a gate giveaway is taking place, fans leaving the exit gate will have their ticket scanned and marked so that they may not receive multiple promotional items.

name: Progressive Field
heading: Smoking
passage: Progressive Field is a non-smoking facility in accordance with the laws of the state of Ohio. Fans are not permitted to smoke or use tobacco products anywhere on Progressive Field property. Electornic Cigarettes, "E-Cigarettes", Vapr Cigarettes, or any device that mimics smoking are also prohibited. Should fans need to smoke, the may use the re-entry gate in Left field to leave the park.

name: Progressive Field
heading: Will Call
passage: Due to renovations of the ballpark, the Box Office will no longer be an option for fans to purchase tickets. All tickets need to be purchased digitally .Effective at the start of the 2024 season, Progressive Field will be a cashless venue. All purchases inside the ballpark must be made with a credit or debit card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or Guards Mobile Wallet. Additionally, and at no charge, fans can convert cash to a prepaid card via reverse ATM machines that can be used for purchases inside and outside the ballpark.

name: Progressive Field
heading: Frequently Asked Questions
passage: What is Guards Wallet and how does it work? Guards Wallet is a centralized payment system integrated into the MLB Ballpark app that allows fans to quickly and easily pay for tickets, concessions and merchandise at the ballpark. Fans only need to store their credit card information once, and they can use it for all in-venue purchases without having to re-enter payment details, while also being able to access any value, discounts, or other Club provided benefits. This simplifies the in-venue purchasing process by providing a single payment method for food and merchandise while streamlining transactions, reducing friction, and allowing fans to focus more on enjoying the game rather than worrying about utilizing multiple payment methods for one transaction.

heading: Champions Monument Plaza
passage: Champions Plaza and the Champions Moment Monument, located outside Gate 4, celebrates the 2005 World Series Champion White Sox and our fans. The diamond-shaped plaza consists of a limited number of bricks inscribed with personalized fan messages (Bricks are no longer available for purchase) , surrounded by engraved pavers commemorating great moments and players in White Sox history. The granite and bronze sculpture that stands at the heart of the plaza depicts and highlights key plays, players and moments of the team's amazing march through October of the Championship 2005 season. The plaza and sculpture were unveiled in April 2008.

name: Raymond James Stadium
heading: PARKING +
passage: Parking is available on a first-come, first-served basis. There are approximately 10,000 spots on-site, as well as 15,000 off-site. Patrons pay for parking upon entrance into the lot. All parking lots require cashless payment. All vehicles that enter RJS property are subject to search. Service Dogs in Training are recognized by the Ohio Revised Code and are permitted. Service dogs in training must be under control and have a liability insurance policy provided by the non-profit agency sponsoring the training. Typically, puppy rearing (under six months of age) focused on socialization and general obedience training is not considered Service Animal Training. Emotional Support Animals may be permitted at Ohio State facilities as a reasonable accommodation. Requests must be reviewed by the University ADA Coordinator’s Office. Guests wishing to make a request for an Emotional Support Animal to an event should submit a disability needs form at least two weeks prior to the event they plan to attend. CLICK HERE .

passage: If tickets or passes are being left for you, they will only be left at the box office. Typically these tickets are not available for pickup until doors open on the day of the event. If your tickets/passes are not in will call, please reach out to your point of contact directly. heading: Do you have accessible parking?
passage: There’s accessible parking in both C & D lots. Let the parking staff know that you need accessible parking and they will direct you to these lots. You need to have an accessible placard in order to park, please be advised that parking is limited. Overflow parking is available in Lot A off of Shoreline Blvd. Transportation will be available to assist those with accessible needs to the main entrance. The Accessibility Shuttle pick-up and drop-off zone is located in the northwest corner of Lot A, near the Shoreline Blvd & Bill Graham Pkwy/North Road intersection.

heading: Prohibited & Permitted Items
passage: Service Animal Policy: A service animal is a dog or a miniature horse that has been individually trained to perform tasks directly related to a person’s disability. The guest and their service animal may be asked to leave if the animal is “out of control” or not housebroken. Animals must be on a leash, harness, or other type of restraint at all times unless the owner is unable to retain an animal on a leash due to a disability. The owner must be in full control of the animal at all times. The care and supervision of the animal is solely the responsibility of the owner. Service animals are not required to wear a vest. Please ask any of our Guest Experience Staff for directions to the animal relief area.

name: SoFi Stadium

passage: For NFL games, SoFi Stadium parking lots will open 4 to 5 hours before kickoff. Entry gates open 2-3 hours prior to kickoff. Please plan on arriving as soon as parking gates open to avoid traffic delays!

name: SoFi Stadium

passage: For concerts and non-NFL games, SoFi Stadium parking lots open 3 to 4 hours prior to event start time. Entry gates open 1-2 hours prior to event start time. Please plan on arriving as soon as parking gates open to avoid traffic delays.

name: SoFi Stadium
heading: SoFi Stadium Hyundai Parking Zones & Maps
passage: It is imperative that guests download the digital parking pass into their smartphone applications and are ready to show it to parking staff at the designated checkpoints. All parking passes will be color coded to match the parking zone. Guests must enter the correct entry gate to the assigned parking zones. The lounge has tiered standing-room drink rails facing the field, several high-top tables, and a cabana-style seating area. The entire area also featuees overhead radiant heaters.

passage: There are 13 public elevators located throughout Target Field. Elevators 1 & 2 are in the Administrative Office building near Gate 6. Elevators 3 & 4 are located across from Section 125. name: Target Field
heading: Entry Guidelines
passage: Aerosols and Self-Defense Sprays may not be carried into Target Field. These items may be stored for free at any entry gate and picked-up at that same gate upon leaving Target Field.

name: Target Field
heading: Entry Guidelines
passage: For the general safety of all guests the following items are not allowed into Target Field: ball retrievers, balloons, bats, beach balls, boom boxes, brooms, fireworks, flasks, Frisbees, coolers, inflatables, laser pointers, lawn chairs, noise-making devices, weapons, wooden sticks, or rods. Small whiskbrooms and small souvenir bats are permitted. Guests will have the option of surrendering the item at the gate, leaving and then returning without the prohibited item prior to entering the ballpark, or storing the item in a locker outside Gate 6 prior to entering the ballpark. Surrendered items will not be returned to guests.

name: Target Field
heading: Firearms
passage: The Minnesota Twins prohibit firearms from being carried into Target Field, even for guests with valid conceal-and-carry permits. The only exception to this policy is for licensed Public Law Enforcement officials. Law Enforcement Officers will be required to check-in with Law Enforcement personnel at the gates and present valid Law Enforcement credentials. Firearms may not be stored in the lockers outside of Gate 6.

name: Target Field
heading: Re-entry
passage: Guests may not leave Target Field and re-enter once they have entered the facility.

name: Target Field

passage: Target Field is a tobacco and cannabis-free facility. Tobacco and cannabis use is not allowed anywhere within Target Field or its appurtenant areas. This includes the ballpark itself, Target Plaza, the Promenade behind the ballpark, and the 5th and 7th Street sidewalks adjacent to Target Field. The use of vaporizers of any sort is also prohibited at Target Field. There is no re-entry at Target Field.

name: Target Field
heading: Contactless Ordering and Payments
passage: The MLB Ballpark app provides guests the ability to order and purchase food, beverage, and merchandise throughout Target Field directly from their mobile device. The app will automatically provide menus and items from the closest concessions and/or retail locations to the guest’s ticketed seat, while also allowing the guest to order from any food, beverage, or retail location throughout Target Field. Pre-packaged order pick up from separate, designated “grab-and-go” stations will complete the contactless dining and/or retail experience. The mobile wallet function within the MLB Ballpark app supports all major credit/debit cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay.

heading: Service Animals
passage: Service animals are defined by the ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) as dogs or miniature horses that are trained to do work to perform tasks related to people with disabilities. The work or task the service animal is trained to do must directly relate to the person's disability. Service Animals must be housebroken. Service Animals are required to behave and not repeatedly bark, growl, jump up on or lunge at other guests or employees. Corrective action must be taken if the service animal is not behaving appropriately.

name: The Pavilion at Star Lake
heading: Service Animals
passage: Dogs whose sole function is to provide comfort or emotional support do not qualify as service animals under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Comfort animals, emotional support animals, and therapy dogs are not listed as service animals under Title III of the ADA. This also applies to the other species of animals wild or domestic, trained, or untrained. The ADA requires the service animal to be under the control of the handler. This may include using a harness, leash, or other tether. Our venue employees are not required to provide for, the care, or supervision of a service animal, including cleaning up after it. Service Animals must remain on the floor and are not allowed on dining chairs, bars, or tables in our food and beverage locations. Live Nation and our operating partners have the right to deny access to a dog that disrupts our operations.

passage: Due to liability-related concerns UCLA has made the decision to align with all of the other events at the stadium and not offer a shuttle service. As a result the courtesy shuttle program is no longer available for UCLA games. The Rose Bowl is compliant with ADA regulations and has the required inventory of ADA parking in lots B, D, and F on a first come first served basis. Once those spots are filled, individuals are directed to the to the next closest available lots. In addition ADA accessible vehicle drop off and pick up is located in Lot B as well as Access Services (www.accessla.org). The Rose Bowl Stadium has wheelchair assistance before, during and after an event on a first come first served basis for movement from the stadium gates to seating locations. Please call (626) 400-5119 to arrange for wheelchair assistance. Individuals that need a wheelchair for the entire event should bring their own as the Rose Bowl’s are intended for transportation assistance only.

heading: PROHIBITED ITEMS
passage: Are service animals allowed in the venue? Only service animals are permitted at the Greek Theatre. The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) defines a service animal as any dog, such as a guide dog or signal dog that is individually trained to provide assistance to an individual with a disability. This includes psychiatric service animals that are individually trained to provide service to individuals with psychiatric or neurological disabilities, such as preventing or interrupting impulsive or destructive behaviors. Service animals must be harnessed, leashed or tethered at all times, unless special circumstances exist, and will be required to rest in the seating area of the individual with a disability, rather than in the aisle. A guest whose service animal poses a threat to the safety of other guests and employees, or whose animal is not housebroken, may be asked to escort the animal off the premises.

passage: Bud Walton Express (Begins 90 min before tip) & Muss Bus (begins 2 hours before tip) There are two complimentary shuttle services for men’s basketball games. This loop will take approximately 20 minutes. • Fans are highly encouraged the use of Lot 72 on the north side of the Frank Broyles Center at Razorback Stadium for convenient free public parking as well as additional ADA parking. The “Bud Walton Express” will pick up and drop off from Lot 44 on both Razorback Road and Stadium Drive.

heading: How do you get to Carnegie Hall?
passage: The answer to this question inspired a well-known joke. The punch line is often attributed to violinist Jascha Heifetz or pianist Arthur Rubinstein, sometimes to an anonymous musician or taxi driver, and once even to a beatnik, who, in a 1960 telling, replied “Practice, man, practice.” At some point, the line was given a triple flourish: “Practice, practice, practice.”

name: Union Transfer
heading: FAQs
passage: I have “Will Call” tickets, what does that mean? Can you send me my tickets in advance instead? “Will Call” tickets are those that are designated for pick-up at the venue on the day of the event, rather than being sent in advance. Unfortunately, tickets that are designated as “Will Call” are not transferable and can only be picked up by the person whose name is on the ticket w/ ID. This is a security measure to ensure that only the person who purchased the tickets is able to attend the event. We can not change the delivery method / re-issue tickets electronically. We understand that it can be inconvenient to pick up your tickets at the venue on the day of the show. However, we typically do not have long lines for Will Call ticket pickup (typically less than 50 customers throughout the night) and our staff is well-trained and efficient at getting customers their tickets quickly. You can pick up your Will Call tickets starting two hours before doors open (usually at 5pm) on the day of the event.

passage: All patrons, regardless of age, are required to have a ticket in order to enter the venue. name: Saenger Theatre
heading: Accessibility Statement – United States
passage: ATG Entertainment is committed to maintaining compliant websites and online services, and to providing an online environment that is accessible to all visitors. This commitment aligns with Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act (29 U.S.C. §794d), and applicable implementing regulations, as well as the recommendations outlined in the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG).

name: Saenger Theatre
heading: Accessibility Statement – United States
passage: We use industry-standard accessibility methods and tools to achieve this. For example, the UserWay Website Accessibility Widget, available on our Sites(s), is powered by a dedicated accessibility server. The widget provides user-triggered enhancements that allow visitors to improve the site’s accessibility. When selected, these features can increase font size, pause animations, adjust colour contrast, and more. Users can choose combinations that best suit their needs, in line with WCAG Level AAA guidelines.

name: Saenger Theatre
heading: Accessibility Statement – United States
passage: Additionally, we enable Automated Remediation Technology (ART) for all visitors. ART does not detect the use of assistive technologies; rather, it enhances accessibility for all site visitors by deploying remediation capabilities. These methods comply with the applicable version of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) established by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), the primary international standards organization for the internet.

name: Saenger Theatre
heading: Accessibility Statement – United States
passage: As part of our commitment to accessibility, we also partner with Audioeye to ensure our continued compliance. Through this partnership, we have conducted and continue to conduct accessibility audits of our online services, and have remediated, and continue to remediate any issues identified during these audits.

Discover all available facilities, including lockers, bars, and restrooms, and get a clear overview of where the box office and various entrances are located. This way, you’ll arrive well-prepared and know exactly where to go.

name: Sportpaleis
heading: Wandel virtueel door de AFAS Dome
passage: Wil je de AFAS Dome al eens ontdekken vóór je bezoek? Met onze 360° tour wandel je virtueel door en rond de volledige venue. Je kan alle faciliteiten bekijken, zoals de lockers, bars en toiletten, en je krijgt een duidelijk overzicht van waar de kassa en de verschillende ingangen zich bevinden. Zo kom je goed voorbereid toe en weet je meteen waar je moet zijn.

name: Sportpaleis
heading: Promenez-vous virtuellement dans l’AFAS Dome

Explorez toutes les installations disponibles, comme les casiers, les bars et les toilettes, et repérez facilement l’emplacement du guichet et des différentes entrées. Vous arriverez ainsi bien préparé et saurez exactement où vous rendre.

name: Sportpaleis
heading: Ouverture des portes
passage: Quelques jours avant l'événement, vous trouverez les informations relatives aux horaires en bas de la page des détails. heading: 1. Personal data and information collected
passage: When you purchase a ticket, you enter into a contract with us. In order to be able to execute this contract, we collect your personal data which enables us to manage your ticket order: payment processing, ticket delivery, invoicing, sending of the confirmation e-mail, customer service, communication of information about the Event, communication of information and reimbursement in the event of cancellation or postponement of the Event, export of data for access control at the entrance to the Event, etc. The name and surname of a member of our staff may be used for this purpose. The surname and first name of a ticket holder may be different from those of the purchaser of the order. For this reason, we advise you to obtain his or her prior consent to communicate this information, since we need to process it for the purposes described above.
